headline: India Smashes Solar Record With 27 GW in Six Months
meta_description: India installed 27 GW of solar power in the first half of 2026, a 50% jump from the previous year, as renewables dominate new capacity.
summary_short: India installed a record 27 GW of solar power in just six months of 2026, marking a 50% surge and cementing solar's dominance in the grid.
body:
India installed a record 27 gigawatts of solar power in the first six months of 2026, a remarkable 50% increase from the same period the previous year. The surge underscores how rapidly the country is pivoting toward clean energy as it expands its power grid.

Solar now accounts for 76% of all new power capacity being added across India. This near-total dominance of renewables in new installations signals a fundamental shift in how the country meets its growing energy demand. Where coal and fossil fuels once governed India's energy mix, solar installations now lead by an overwhelming margin.

The acceleration reflects both India's ambitious climate commitments and the plummeting cost of solar technology, making it the cheapest option for new power generation. As the world's most populous country grapples with energy needs and air quality challenges, this record offers a concrete example of renewable energy scaling at the pace climate science demands.
quick_facts: 27 GW of solar installed in India's first half of 2026
Solar represents 76% of all new power capacity added
